context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud under strict latency and compliance constraints. It evaluates transactions in real-time and provides a case management interface for fraud analysts.

## Key Elements
- External Payment Gateway and Fraud Analysts (Users/Systems)
- AWS API Gateway with ingress schema validation (Container)
- AWS ECS on Fargate stateless scoring engine (Container)
- Amazon Aurora Serverless case management database (Container)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock and Glacier Vault Lock audit store (Container)
- AWS SNS and PagerDuty alerting (Container)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to AWS API Gateway via HTTPS/HTTP/2 using gRPC/JSON payloads
- ECS Fargate to Amazon Aurora Serverless via TLS for case management data
- Scoring Engine to Amazon S3 via HTTPS for local model artifact loading
- System to Amazon S3 via AWS SDK for tamper-evident cryptographic audit logs
- System to PagerDuty via AWS SNS for operational alerts

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS on Fargate: chosen for stateless scaling and low operational overhead
- Amazon Aurora Serverless: selected for elastic relational case management storage
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock and Glacier: provides cost-effective, tamper-evident 7-year audit retention
- AWS API Gateway: handles ingress validation, rate limiting, and circuit breaking
- Terraform and AWS Config: automates Infrastructure as Code and policy-as-code compliance

## Rationale
This architecture uses vertically scalable managed services to easily achieve sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS within a €25k monthly budget. It minimizes operational toil for a three-engineer team while satisfying rigorous PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability constraints.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides a case management interface for analysts. It processes payments securely while maintaining strict compliance, auditability, and budgetary constraints.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts (System Users)
- External Payment Gateway (External System)
- API Gateway / Ingestion Service (Container)
- Scoring Engine (Container)
- Case Management & Admin UI (Container)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock (Storage)
- Amazon SQS (Message Queue)
- AWS ECS with Fargate (Orchestration)

## Relationships
- External Payment Gateway sends authorization requests to API Gateway / Ingestion Service via HTTPS/REST.
- API Gateway / Ingestion Service forwards scoring payloads to Scoring Engine via gRPC/Protobuf.
- Scoring Engine writes tamper-evident audit logs to Amazon S3 with Object Lock via AWS SDK.
- Fraud Analysts interact with Case Management & Admin UI via HTTPS/REST.
- Scoring Engine delegates asynchronous failure events to Amazon SQS.

## Technology Stack
- AWS Fargate: Container orchestration to maintain low operational overhead for a three-person team.
- Rust, Go, or Java with embedded ML runtimes: High-performance backend technologies to ensure P99 latency below 50 ms.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: WORM storage to meet the 7-year tamper-evident audit requirement.
- Amazon SQS: Dead-letter queue for reliable asynchronous event processing without blocking primary transaction paths.
- OpenAPI/Protobuf: Strict API contract definitions to prevent schema drift between services.

## Rationale
The architecture limits container count and leverages AWS managed services to minimize operational toil for a three-person team within a €25,000 monthly budget. High-performance runtimes, circuit breakers, and rolling deployments ensure strict P99 latency, high availability, and PCI-DSS compliance.

API Gateway / Ingestion Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud prior to approval and provides a case management interface for analysts. It operates on AWS within a strict infrastructure budget and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance requirements.

## Key Elements
- External Payment Gateway
- API Gateway / Ingestion Service
- Scoring Engine
- Case Management & Admin UI
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock
- Amazon SQS
- AWS ECS with Fargate

## Relationships
- External Payment Gateway -> API Gateway / Ingestion Service: Sends authorization requests via HTTPS/REST
- API Gateway / Ingestion Service -> Scoring Engine: Forwards scoring payloads via gRPC/Protobuf

## Technology Stack
- Go: Selected for the API Gateway to achieve sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 req/s while avoiding garbage collection pauses.
- OpenAPI: Used at the edge for strict, declarative schema validation and contract-first development.
- AWS ECS with Fargate: Runs containerized services to meet the 25,000 EUR monthly budget with minimal operational overhead for a 3-engineer team.
- Prometheus: Provides managed metrics scraping for HTTP request rates and gRPC upstream latencies.

## Rationale
The architecture prioritizes high-throughput, low-latency Go microservices deployed on serverless AWS containers to satisfy strict performance and availability constraints. Strict tokenization, circuit breaking, and automated data masking ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and auditability within a small team capacity.

Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at scale and provides a case management interface for manual reviews. It ensures high availability, strict P99 latency compliance, and tamper-evident auditing within a fixed cloud budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts: Human operators reviewing suspicious payments via the Case Management UI.
- External Payment Gateway: Sends payment authorization payloads to the system.
- API Gateway / Ingestion Service: Ingests external HTTP/gRPC requests, validates schemas, and forwards payloads.
- Scoring Engine: Core container evaluating fraud risk via embedded ML runtimes.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Stores immutable, tamper-evident audit logs.
- Amazon SQS: Queues asynchronous failure and audit events.
- AWS ECS with Fargate: Serverless container execution environment.

## Relationships
- External Payment Gateway -> API Gateway / Ingestion Service: Forwards authorization requests [HTTPS/gRPC]
- API Gateway / Ingestion Service -> Scoring Engine: Forwards scoring payloads [gRPC/Protobuf]
- Scoring Engine -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Writes tamper-evident audit logs [AWS SDK]
- Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS: Delegates asynchronous failure events [AWS SDK / Message Queue]

## Technology Stack
- Rust or Go: Selected for the Scoring Engine to eliminate garbage collection pauses and meet the 50 ms P99 latency target at 3,000 TPS.
- Protobuf: Used for efficient, schema-validated binary communication between the API Gateway and Scoring Engine.
- Memory-Mapped Files: Enables zero-downtime model weight hot-reloading.
- AWS ECS with Fargate: Provides scalable, serverless container hosting within budget.
- Prometheus: Powers real-time telemetry, latency histograms, and circuit breaker health metrics.

## Rationale
This architecture uses high-performance compiled languages and serverless AWS infrastructure to meet strict sub-50ms latency and 3,000 TPS throughput constraints within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Stateless container design, circuit breakers, and local fail-safes guarantee high availability and PCI-DSS compliance while remaining operable by a three-person engineering team.

Case Management & Admin UI.analysis:
## Overview
[The Case Management & Admin UI system provides fraud analysts with a secure interface to review suspicious payment authorizations, manage cases, and update fraud rules without downtime. It is deployed on AWS to maintain strict PCI-DSS compliance and support 7-year auditability.]

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analysts
* Case Management & Admin UI (Web UI)
* Backend-For-Frontend (BFF) Container (AWS Fargate)
* Single Page Application (SPA) Frontend (AWS CloudFront / Amazon S3)
* AWS Cognito
* Amazon CloudWatch

## Relationships
* Fraud Analysts -> Case Management & Admin UI (SPA): Accesses interface [HTTPS]
* SPA -> BFF Container: Communicates via API calls [HTTPS/REST]
* BFF Container -> AWS Cognito: Authenticates users and manages sessions [OIDC/HTTPS]
* BFF Container -> Downstream Services: Fetches and updates case data [HTTPS/REST]
* BFF and SPA -> Amazon CloudWatch: Emits structured logs and distributed traces [AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
* AWS CloudFront and Amazon S3: Hosts the SPA for cost-effective global delivery
* React or Vue: Lightweight frontend framework for high-performance rendering
* Ant Design or MUI: Pre-built component library to accelerate development with a 3-engineer team
* AWS Fargate (ECS): Runs the BFF container to securely handle session management and API aggregation
* AWS Cognito: Managed identity provider for secure Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
* Pact and Playwright: Automated contract and end-to-end testing frameworks for CI/CD pipeline reliability

## Rationale
[This architecture leverages serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS compliance. The BFF pattern and secure cookie management protect sensitive payment data while ensuring robust auditability.]

- Case Management & Admin UI: Web interface for fraud analysts to review flagged transactions.

- API Gateway / Ingestion Service -> Scoring Engine: Delegates transaction payloads via gRPC/Protobuf.

- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management & Admin UI: Accesses review cases via HTTPS.

## Technology Stack

- Rust / Go / Java: Selected for core microservices to guarantee sub-50ms P99 performance at scale.

## Rationale
The architecture maximizes automation and uses serverless container orchestration to operate securely and reliably with a three-engineer team under a fixed 25,000 EUR monthly budget. AWS native services and strict latency optimizations ensure PCI-DSS compliance and sub-50ms performance without exceeding operational capacity.
